# Product moments

<!-- Generated by `python3 scripts/pick.py --write-docs references` from assets/library/techniques.json. Edit the JSON, then regenerate. -->

A real product doing its job on screen: prompts, results, diffs, scrubs and native transitions shown, never listed. 21 entries, by category and role. The [index](../technique-library.md) lists every family and each category's house rule.

### A product moment in one camera

`pd-product-moment-one-camera` · ui choreography · signature · energy high · launch, update, feature

One continuous camera over one desk: the panel enters front-loaded on a tilted plane, the cursor swings upright and presses, the one spring pops the container open, the next card lands while the panel steps back, everything unfolds into the dashboard on one shared curve, pictures develop, a flick lands on the item that matters and a live counter is cut mid-count.

- **Build:** Design the overview layout in screen px at the pull-back framing with the copy cell left empty, map it to desk px; each beat is a camera key (scale + anchor of that layout) joined by strongInOut / liftOut reframes and linear creeps. Beat 1 <Card enter lean>, cursorState(tilt swing, click ring); beat 2 press() + springBox() (SPRING_CLASS = the container) and stepValue() badges; beat 3 cardArrive + demote centred on it, <Bubbles anchor=bottom> above a composer; beat 4 <Bento> with tile contents fading up as boxes open, <Develop> thumbnails, the light pool brightened once; beat 5 flickState (declares -> CAMERA_BLUR) and countLinear, hard cut mid-count.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards`, `fx/Cursor.cursorState`, `fx/Bubbles`, `fx/Develop`, `fx/Scroll.flickState`, `fx/Roll.countLinear`
- **Timing:** About 9 s at 60 fps plus a 1 s end card: enter 40 f, press at 2 s, spring 8 f after the press, card lands at 3.2 s, unfold at 5.4 s (44 f), flick at 7.5 s, cut at 8.9 s. One calm fragment per beat, at line size or bigger, in the empty cell.
- **Use when:** The signature shot of a launch film, or each change of an update video (one moment per change, built UI or a supplied screenshot card with its one live element rebuilt).
- **Avoid when:** A film whose product is not a screen (use the camera and type devices).

### Agent status beat, then streamed answer

`pd-agent-status-then-answer` · product demo · workhorse · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough, vertical

The product's tiny working status is shown at hero size, as a black capsule with a spinner and a typed label or as bare headline type, holds for a beat with a looping ellipsis or shimmer, then dissolves as the answer streams in.

- **Build:** Build the status as a capsule (height ≈ 8.4% of frame, border-radius 999 px, C.ink fill, an 8-dot spinner stepping 45° every 6 f, label typed with TypeOn) or as bare type at 72-100 px with a clock or spinner glyph at cap height, its trailing word arriving in C.accent and relaxing to ink with mixColor over 24 f. Keep the hold alive with a looping ellipsis '.'.repeat(1 + (Math.floor(fd(f) / 16) % 3)) and a one-hue shimmer (background-clip: text over three lightness stops of the label grey, band ≈ 120 px, position linear in f), while the camera settles 1.62 → 1 with lmix over 56 f on E.outSoft. Dissolve the status over 12 f on E.smooth, then stream the answer with TypeOn at about 60 cps, the newest three characters at 0.3/0.6/0.85 opacity and each new character in the accent relaxing to ink over 12 f. When the status itself is the payoff, type it, hold 30 f and dim it to C.mute over 12 f instead of streaming.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Keep the same beat but build every decoration from one hue: a flat C.ink capsule with a plain soft neutral drop shadow instead of coloured light blobs behind it, a dot spinner or clock glyph instead of a sparkle icon, a shimmer made of three lightness stops of one grey instead of a multi-hue sweep, and an accent-to-ink trail on the newest characters instead of a multi-colour wake. The full look relies on gradient, sparkle, glow; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Label types in about 30 f (40 f at headline size); hold 60-74 f with the ellipsis stepping every 16 f and one shimmer sweep per 60 f (≈ 20 px/f); camera 1.62 → 1 over 56 f on E.outSoft; dissolve 12 f; stream ≈ 1 character per frame (41 characters in about 42 f); payoff variant: hold 30 f, dim 12 f.
- **Use when:** An AI or agent product needs its invisible work made visible, and a moment of anticipation before the payoff.
- **Avoid when:** The product is not autonomous; the hold would run past about 74 f; a second status beat in the same film.

### Change applied as a visible diff

`pd-diff-hunks-apply` · product demo · workhorse · energy calm · feature, walkthrough

A proposed edit lands in a code or document view as a diff: outgoing lines strike through and fold away, incoming lines open in place with a marker in the gutter, and the view steps hunk by hunk before the change is accepted.

- **Build:** Render the file as live lines from data (FONT.mono for code, the text face for prose) beside a gutter of line numbers, and drive each hunk from its own start frame. An outgoing line first gets a 1.5 px C.mute strike that draws left to right over 8 f on E.ui (scaleX 0 → 1 from the left) while its text dims to C.mute; 6 f later it folds from line height to 0 over 12 f on E.ui, its opacity gone in the first 8 f. On that same frame an incoming slot opens from 0 to line height over 12 f on E.ui (the lines below are pushed through the computed layout), a 3 px C.accent bar appears in the gutter on its first frame, the new text appears whole once the slot is 70% open, and a C.accent 10% row tint relaxes to clear over 36 f while the bar stays; line numbers below recompute on fd(f) and are never tweened. Step to the next hunk 60-90 f later with the anchor camera (lc to a Shot centred on it) over 48 f on E.glide, keeping each hop under about 300 px (peak ≈ 19 px/f) and hard-cutting on the same axis to anything farther; on Accept (a Cursor press with pressAt on the button) every gutter bar fades over 12 f on E.smooth and the clean file holds under breath(t, 0.02).
- **Timing:** Strike 8 f on E.ui; fold 12 f on E.ui starting 6 f later; slot open 12 f on E.ui with the text in at 70%; tint relax 36 f; hunks 60-90 f apart, camera hop 48 f on E.glide (≤ 300 px); accept fade 12 f; final hold 36-48 f under a 2% breath; at most three hunks.
- **Use when:** AI coding or writing assistants and review, versioning or migration tools, when the claim is 'it changes exactly the right lines and shows you which'.
- **Avoid when:** The code is unreadable at frame size (macro in first), or the change needs more than three hunks (show a summary instead); never give removals a second colour.

### Command runs, output prints in bursts

`pd-terminal-burst-output` · product demo · workhorse · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, launch

A command is typed at human speed and entered; the terminal answers machine-fast, printing whole lines in uneven bursts with a stepping spinner and a progress bar, and ends on a single success line.

- **Build:** Set the terminal in FONT.mono at no less than TYPE.ui size, in a C.ink2 window with a 1.5 px edge, with every line laid out from data on a fixed line height, and keep breath(t, 0.02) on the camera for the whole run. Type the command with TypeOn at a human 30 cps with fade 0 (keys appear whole), hold the caret 10 f, then enter on a quiet tick. Output never types: each line appears whole on its own frame from a hand-written schedule of uneven bursts (for example 3 lines on consecutive frames, a 14 f gap, 5 lines 2 f apart, a 22 f gap), decided on fd(f), with the newest line in C.white and older ones relaxing to C.mute over 24 f; once text reaches the bottom row, each burst scrolls the content up by its total height as one move over max(6, 0.14 × distance) f on E.ui, so text never passes 20 px/f. A working line steps the four-glyph ASCII spinner (bar, slash, dash, backslash) every 4 f beside a text progress bar whose filled cells advance on fd(prog(f, a, a + 60, E.smooth) × cells), and the run ends on one success line whose check mark and key word arrive in C.accent and stay, followed by a fresh prompt with the caret blinking 30 f on, 30 f off.
- **Timing:** Command at 30 cps, caret hold 10 f; bursts of 2-6 lines 1-2 f apart with 10-24 f gaps (40-80 lines in 120-180 f reads machine-fast); line relax 24 f; burst scroll max(6, 0.14 × px) f on E.ui; spinner step 4 f; progress bar 60 f on E.smooth; success line held 48-60 f under the breath with the caret blinking 30/30.
- **Use when:** Developer tools, CLIs, infrastructure and build products, where the contrast between a human-typed command and machine-fast output is the speed claim.
- **Avoid when:** The audience is not technical, or the output itself must be read line by line (show the result screen instead); never type the output.

### Device rises already moving

`pd-device-rise-on-cut` · product demo · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough, vertical

A phone or app window enters from below already travelling on the cut frame and decelerates into place near centre while the whole shot slowly scales down.

- **Build:** Drive the device group's translateY = tw(f, cut − 1, cut + 43, rise, 0, E.out) with rise 140-160 px, so it already moves about 20 px/f on the cut frame (prog is 0 on its first frame, hence cut − 1); no fade-in, since the cut hides the start, and the shadow travels with the device. Under it, scale the whole shot 1 → 0.9 over 48 f on E.outSoft; a desaturated photo backdrop (grayscale(1) contrast(1.1) brightness(0.7)) keeps the device the only colour. When the device must push a title off screen without a cut, rise it from a full frame height below over 48 f on E.glide (peak ≈ 59 px/f at 31%, motion blur on), fade the title on E.smooth starting 16 f before the device moves, and keep the device above the title in z. For anticipation, peek first: 170 px in 14 f on E.out, hover 4 f, then launch the rest on E.whip over 40 f (peak under 70 px/f) and drift the scale 1 → 0.93 over 60 f.
- **Timing:** On a cut: 140-160 px over 44 f on E.out, first frame ≈ 6.2 × rise / 44 (about 20-23 px/f), 75% of the travel by f9, settled by f44; shot scale 1 → 0.9 over 48 f on E.outSoft. Over a title: ≈ 1,000 px in 48 f on E.glide, title fade 36 f starting 16 f early. Peek variant: 14 f peek, 4 f hover, 40 f launch on E.whip, 60 f scale drift.
- **Use when:** The first product shot after a type card or a photo, when the previous shot's energy should carry straight into the product.
- **Avoid when:** The device is already on screen; a calm film where a 20 px/f arrival feels pushy; it would be the third rise in a row (vary with a tilt or a pull-back).

### Edit with the product's own UI

`pd-ui-native-transitions` · product demo · workhorse · energy medium · walkthrough, feature, launch

Instead of cuts, the film moves between product areas the way the app does: a window recedes to a corner, a sheet slides up, a popover pops from its anchor, a button or card unfolds into a full panel.

- **Build:** Model the app as stacked layers in one scene, park the cursor on the control that would trigger each change 6 f before the press, and use the matching native behaviour instead of a cut. Minimize: transform-origin at the trigger corner, scale 1 → 0.7 on E.in over 22 f while opacity falls 1 → 0 over its last 12 f on E.smooth (the far corner is mostly gone before it passes 60 px/f), with the next layer 4 f later. Sheet: translateY 100% → 0 of the window over 52 f on E.glide, clipped to the window. Popover: scale 0.5 → 1 from the trigger point over 12 f on E.outSoft with opacity over its first 4 f, then a 20-40 f camera reframe starting 2 f later. Launch: the sidebar glides left 31% of frame width over 96 f on E.smooth while the main canvas mounts whole on the trigger frame and its greeting starts typing on that frame. Unfold: one element interpolates rect and border-radius from the button or card to the full panel over 28 f on E.rest (longer for a big panel: at least edge travel / 20 f, so no edge passes about 70 px/f) and its title FLIPs to the header slot (scale 1 → 0.6), flying faded whenever it moves faster than 20 px/f; the old content fades out over the first 12 f, the panel content fades in 8 f after the morph peaks, and the stage behind dims over 24 f (a RackFocus at 40 px for a blurred desktop).
- **Timing:** Generic chain: exit on E.in 22 f, gap 4 f, entrance on E.out 52 f. Minimize 22 f; sheet 52 f (peak ≈ 50 px/f); popover 12 f plus a 20-40 f reframe; launch slide 96 f (peak ≈ 18 px/f); unfold 28 f on E.rest (at least edge travel / 20 f), content in 8 f after the peak, stage dim 24 f.
- **Use when:** Walkthroughs across several product areas; any film where each transition can also demonstrate how the product navigates.
- **Avoid when:** A purely conceptual or type-led film; desktop chrome that is not part of the brand world; more than one native transition every 3 s (it starts to feel like a screen recording).

### Fast prompt at true scale

`pd-fast-prompt-true-scale` · product demo · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough, vertical

The real prompt bar fills with a long, honest instruction in about a second at full legible size, the card growing as lines wrap, then the text is sent up into a chat bubble.

- **Build:** Type with TypeOn (src/fx/TypeOn.tsx), either time-boxed (dur 68, ease E.linear, so prompts of any length finish in 68 f and every ask beat keeps its length) or at a fixed 50-72 cps; pre-fill the first word so frame 1 already shows text, and draw the newest three characters at 0.3/0.6/0.85 opacity, each arriving in C.accent and relaxing to ink over 12 f. Grow the card from the measured text box: width ≈ 67% → 77% of frame over the first 24 f, then one line height over 12 f on E.out at each wrap, decided on fd(f). Keep the frame alive with breath(t, 0.025) from src/lib/camera.ts on the camera; the caret is solid while typing and blinks 16 f on / 16 f off only once done. On the send press the composer text fades out over 12 f while the bubble rises 12-20 px through arrive() and fades in over 16-18 f, starting 4 f later.
- **Timing:** Time box 68 f, or 50-72 cps (0.8-1.2 characters per frame); card width 24 f, +1 line per wrap in 12 f on E.out; read hold after typing at least 36 f + 6 f per word, kept alive by the breath; send: 12 f out, bubble 16-18 f in with a 4 f offset.
- **Use when:** An AI, search or command product whose real input is the story; showing a real task without a dull typing wait.
- **Avoid when:** The prompt runs past about 100 characters (cut it); a human-paced beat is the point (use 30 cps with human rhythm); the product is not input-driven.

### Ghost suggestion accepted with a key

`pd-ghost-suggestion-accept` · product demo · workhorse · energy calm · feature, walkthrough, launch

As someone types, the product proposes the rest of the line as pale ghost text after the caret; a small key chip appears, the key is pressed, and the ghost text inks in left to right as the caret jumps to its end.

- **Build:** Type the user's prefix with TypeOn at a human 30 cps; 12 f after the last key, draw the suggestion as one span starting at the prefix's caretX from typeOn(), in the same font and baseline and in C.mute, appearing whole on one frame (or streaming at 2 characters per frame for a longer block), so nothing already typed reflows. Twelve px past its last glyph (or under the line end if that would cross the field edge), mount a key chip (a FONT.mono label at 0.6 em in a 6 px-radius box with a 1.5 px C.line border and a 3 px bottom edge) on spr(f, s, SPR.micro) from scale 0.8 with opacity over 6 f, and keep the 30-40 f wait alive with breath(t, 0.02) on the camera. On ACCEPT the chip presses with pressAt (translateY 2 px and its bottom edge 3 → 1 px, both times the press value), and on that frame a recolour front runs through the ghost text, k = fd(prog(f, ACCEPT − 1, ACCEPT + 10, E.linear) × n): each character behind the front switches from C.mute to C.accent on its frame and relaxes to C.ink over 12 f by its own age (mixColor), while the prefix caret is removed (caretOut = ACCEPT) and a caret appears at the suggestion's end on the same frame. The chip fades out over 8 f on E.smooth from ACCEPT + 4; in a multi-line block each line's front starts 3 f after the line above, and a rejection uses the same chip labelled Esc with the ghost text fading out over 8 f on E.smooth.
- **Timing:** Prefix at 30 cps; ghost text 12 f after the last key, whole in 1 f (or 2 characters per frame); chip on SPR.micro with a 6 f fade; wait 30-40 f under a 2% breath; press 4 f down, 8 f recoil; recolour front 10 f per line (lines 3 f apart), accent relax 12 f; chip out over 8 f from ACCEPT + 4; read hold after acceptance 36-48 f.
- **Use when:** An assistant that completes text, code, email or form fields inline: the moment the product does the work is one key away, and the cause (the key) and the effect (the ink) share a frame.
- **Avoid when:** The product generates whole answers rather than inline completions (stream the answer instead), or the suggestion runs past about two lines at readable size; never show more than two accepts in a row.

### Hard swap on the cause frame

`pd-hard-swap-on-cause` · product demo · workhorse · energy medium · any

On a click or selection the product image, view or value changes in one frame with no crossfade, any price or count rolls up from just below its new value, and a physical card can hide the swap in a small 3D kick.

- **Build:** Export the cause frame once (the press of pressAt from src/fx/Cursor.tsx after a hover state shown 6 f earlier, or a selection marker's landing) and switch state on fd(f) >= CAUSE so every motion-blur sub-sample agrees; never crossfade the two states. Re-count numbers with Roll fed countSteps(next − delta, next, CAUSE, 40, E.out), delta about 5-10% of the value, so the digits roll instead of cutting. Punch the swapped object with scale 1 + 0.02 · hitPulse(f − CAUSE, 2, 5). For a print or card beside a list, kick it: perspective 900 px, transform-origin on its left edge, rotateY = 12° · hitPulse(f − CAUSE + 1, 1, 2.5) with skewY 2° on the same envelope and a soft shadow (0 18px 40px rgba(0,0,0,.18)), while the list's selection marker moves 6 f before the swap.
- **Timing:** Swap 1 f on the cause frame; hover 6 f before the press; recount 36-46 f on E.out with 14 f digit rolls; punch attack 2 f, tau 5; kick peaks on the swap frame and settles in 6-8 f; at most one swap per 30 f, 54 f apart in a repeating sequence.
- **Use when:** A choice changes the product instantly: a variant picker, filter, plan selector, theme switch, a canvas that appears whole on launch.
- **Avoid when:** The change is a process the viewer should watch; two numbers would sit half-and-half in place; swaps faster than one per 30 f (the clicks read as a macro).

### List narrows with each keystroke

`pd-live-filter-narrows` · product demo · workhorse · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, launch

A shortcut opens a command palette or search field, and as the query types the list answers every key: non-matching rows fold away, survivors slide up, matched letters ink in, and the highlight rides the top result until Enter.

- **Build:** Open with the shortcut if the product has one: two key chips (FONT.mono labels, 1.5 px C.line border, 3 px bottom edge) appear 4 f apart and press together with pressAt, and on the press frame the palette scales 0.96 → 1 about its top centre with opacity over 10 f on E.outSoft while the app behind racks to 8 px through RackFocus under a 20% C.ink veil over 12 f. Type the query with TypeOn at 30-40 cps and recompute the matches from the data on each key frame (typeFrames(), decided on fd(f)), so the list is a pure function of the characters typed: rows that stop matching fold from row height to 0 over 10 f on E.ui with their opacity gone in the first 6 f, and survivors FLIP to their new slots from the computed list layout over max(12, 0.14 × distance) f on E.ui, so no label passes 20 px/f. In every surviving label the matched characters switch to C.ink on the key frame while the rest drops to C.mute (colour only, never weight, so nothing reflows), and one shared highlight (C.mist, 8 px radius) always sits behind the top result and FLIPs to its new rect over 8 f on E.ui. On Enter (a single chip press) the chosen row takes a C.accent 12% tint for 6 f and the palette closes, scale 1 → 0.98 with opacity out over 8 f on E.smooth, while the result mounts underneath on the press frame.
- **Timing:** Chips 4 f apart, press 4 f down + 8 f recoil; palette 10 f on E.outSoft, backdrop rack and veil 12 f; query 30-40 cps; row fold 10 f on E.ui (opacity 6 f); survivor FLIP max(12, 0.14 × px) f on E.ui; highlight 8 f on E.ui; 4-7 keys narrow 8-10 rows to 1-3; final list held 24-36 f under a 2% breath before Enter; close 8 f.
- **Use when:** Search, command menus, filters and pickers: any product whose speed claim is 'type a few letters and it is there', proving instant results without a spinner.
- **Avoid when:** The rows are illegible at frame size (punch in first), or the query is long (past about 12 characters it becomes a typing beat); do not FLIP more than about ten rows at once.

### One native control as the demo

`pd-single-control-hero` · product demo · workhorse · energy calm · feature, launch, vertical, loop

Instead of a screenshot, the feature is shown as the single control that embodies it (a picker wheel, a toggle, a segmented switch) at large scale, centred, with no chrome, doing only its native interaction.

- **Build:** Build only that control at 3-5x its native size, centred on an empty stage with no app chrome. For a picker, scroll the column with inertia(f, s, 20, 0.975) from src/lib/anim.ts (≈ 790 px, tau ≈ 40 f, starting at the 20 px/f readable-text limit) and style each item from its distance d to the centre line: scale 1.2 − 0.35 · min(d / 375, 1), colour mixColor(C.ink, C.mute, min(d / 375, 1)), opacity 1 → 0.35 on the same ratio. Either cut while it still drifts, or click the chosen item home with SPR.detent. Toggles and segmented controls keep their real geometry (knob 8 f on E.ui, the selected pill gliding between labels on E.glide).
- **Timing:** Shot ≈ 120 f; picker v0 20 px/f, decay 0.975 per frame, an item crossing focus about every 30 f early on and slowing after; detent settle ≈ 12 f; toggle knob 8 f; segment glide 18-24 f.
- **Use when:** A settings, targeting or compatibility claim in a type-led film, where one interaction says it is a real product faster than a full UI.
- **Avoid when:** The feature needs context to make sense; the control is generic (every app has a toggle) and says nothing about the claim.

### Scrub a chart with a live readout

`pd-chart-scrub-readout` · product demo · workhorse · energy calm · feature, walkthrough, launch

The cursor glides across a chart; a hairline and a dot ride the series beneath it and a small readout shows the date and value at that point, stepping from data point to data point until it lands on the one that makes the claim.

- **Build:** Build the chart from data in one SVG and make the scrub a pure function of the cursor's x: move src/fx/Cursor.tsx along a shallow cursorArc (bow 0.05) on E.smooth at 6-10 px/f, and take the active point i as the data point nearest that x, decided on fd(f). Layer back to front: series, a 1.5 px C.line hairline at point i's x, a 6 px solid dot on the series at point i with a 2 px ring in the stage colour, the readout, then the cursor; the hairline and dot snap from point to point as i changes (use 40 or more points so each snap is small; with sparse data let the hairline follow the cursor x and snap only the dot and value). The readout is a small card (8 px radius, C.ink on paper or C.white on ink) with a FONT.mono date in C.mute above the value in tabular figures; it rides along the plot's top edge at the cursor's x, clamped inside the plot so it never flips sides, and its value changes through Roll fed one step per index change (roll 8) so digits roll instead of cutting. The hairline and readout fade in over 6 f as the cursor crosses into the plot, and the scrub ends on the point that carries the claim, where the dot pulses at scale 1 + 0.25 · hitPulse(f − LAND, 2, 6) and the value arrives in C.accent and relaxes to C.ink over 24 f.
- **Timing:** Scrub 90-150 f on E.smooth at 6-10 px/f (the readout never moves faster than the cursor); hairline and readout in over 6 f; value roll 8 f per index change; landing pulse attack 2 f, tau 6; accent relax 24 f; hold on the landing point 36-48 f under a 2% breath.
- **Use when:** Analytics, finance, health or monitoring products whose value is reading any point in history; a calm interaction beat after a fast one.
- **Avoid when:** The chart has no point worth landing on, or the readout is illegible at the framing (punch in to 1.6-2x first); never scrub faster than the readout can be read.

### Supplied screenshots move like built UI

`pd-screenshot-grammar` · product demo · workhorse · energy medium · launch, update, feature

Real product screenshots and product shots enter, unfold, develop and get pushed into with the same grammar as built UI; the one element the film acts on is rebuilt live on top so it can press, spring or count.

- **Build:** <Card image={{ src: staticFile('shot.png'), fit: 'cover', focus: { x, y }, zoom, zoomTo, zoomStart, zoomDur }} enter={...} />; <Bento tiles={[{ A, B, image }]} />; <Develop image={{ src }} />. Supply images at 2x their largest on-screen size; crop the focus onto the feature; overlay the acting element as live UI at the same place and size.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards.Card`, `fx/Cards.Bento`, `fx/Develop`
- **Timing:** As the primitive used; a slow push inside a card zooms x1.05 -> x1.15 over 4 s.
- **Use when:** Any film made from a supplied brand kit or product screenshots; update videos with 2-4 changes.
- **Avoid when:** Screenshots smaller than their on-screen size (they go soft): rebuild those as live UI.

### Before/after drag divider

`pd-before-after-drag-wipe` · product demo · accent · energy medium · feature, launch, walkthrough

The cursor grabs a vertical divider on the product and drags it across, wiping away the old state to reveal the new one in the same layout.

- **Build:** Stack two renders of the same layout: before below, after above, clipped with clip-path inset(0 0 0 X px) where X is the divider's position; draw the divider as a 2 px C.white line (C.ink on paper) with a 40 px round handle holding two small chevrons. The cursor arrives on cursorArc over 36-48 f on E.out, presses the handle (pressAt) and drags it across the product panel on E.smooth over 60 f (≈ 1,100 px, peak ≈ 52 px/f). Optionally it pauses once at the midpoint for up to 24 f under a breath push so both states read side by side. Values that differ between the states change exactly where the divider passes them, because they sit on separate layers, so the halves are never crossfaded.
- **Timing:** Cursor approach 36-48 f on E.out; press 4 f down, 8 f recoil; drag 60 f on E.smooth, or 36 f to the midpoint on E.glide (peak ≈ 46 px/f), a hold of ≤ 24 f, then 36 f on to the edge.
- **Use when:** Redesigns, image or audio cleanup, performance gains, any this-got-better claim with a visible difference.
- **Avoid when:** The two states differ in layout (the wipe then reads as a glitch); the difference is invisible at frame size; the film has no human gesture anywhere else.

### Generated view resolves from soft

`pd-blur-resolve-load` · product demo · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough, loop

A freshly generated window or row appears as a soft, out-of-focus shape over a flat placeholder plate and snaps into crisp UI in about a third of a second.

- **Build:** Mount the finished UI over a flat placeholder plate (C.mist, or C.accent at 12% opacity: one hue only). Render the UI through RackFocus (src/fx/RackFocus.tsx) with blur 20 px and t = 1 − p, p = prog(f, s, s + 20, E.out); fade its opacity 0.6 → 1 and scale it 1.03 → 1 on the same p so the focus pull rides a move, and fade the plate out over the same 20 f on E.smooth. For a list, insert rows one at a time: width 60% → 100% with RackFocus 6 → 0 px over 12 f, siblings pushed down one row over 10 f on E.ui, rows 34-40 f apart; inside an unfolding card, start a row's rack only once 60% of its height is revealed. t must reach 0 by the end, so text lands fully sharp.
- **Timing:** Window: 20 f on E.out (blur 20 → 0 px, opacity 0.6 → 1, scale 1.03 → 1), plate fade 20 f on E.smooth. Rows: 12 f each, push-down 10 f on E.ui, cadence 34-40 f. Card stats row: 12 f, starting once 60% of it is revealed.
- **Use when:** An AI or build step produces a result and it should read as just arrived, without a spinner.
- **Avoid when:** The UI was already on screen (use a state change); more than two resolves in one sequence (it becomes a fog filter); type so small that 12 f of softness hurts legibility.

### Long page flown like a runway

`pd-page-runway-flyover` · product demo · accent · energy high · launch, feature, walkthrough

A whole long page lies on a steeply tilted plane that recedes to a horizon, and the view travels along it faster and faster, so the page reads as one landscape and is cut at full speed.

- **Build:** Lay the whole page out as live components at desktop width inside a runway plane about 75% of frame width and 2x frame height long (overflow hidden), in a full-frame parent with perspective 1200 px and its perspective-origin at frame centre; give the plane transform-origin 50% 100%, rotateX(55deg) and put its bottom edge on the frame's bottom edge, so its far edge recedes to a horizon about 25% down the frame and its sides converge like a runway. Move the page inside the plane, never the camera: translateY = Y0 + 6n + 0.225n² for n = f − s up to 54 (plane speed 6 → 30 px/f), then +36 px per frame to the cut, so content streams toward the viewer and the page's upper sections emerge from the horizon (start with its lower sections on the plane so the hero arrives last); at the near edge the screen speed is about 0.95x the plane speed and the far half moves much slower. Fade the far end with an alpha mask on the plane, mask-image linear-gradient(to top, #000 45%, transparent 95%), so the stage colour swallows the horizon in one hue, and keep the empty stage above the horizon as the caption band, where one short line lands with src/fx/Words.tsx in screen space while the page streams below it. Nothing on the plane is meant to be read: keep the motion-blur pass on for the whole flight and cut on its last, fastest frame into a shot that opens moving the same way.
- **Timing:** Flight 80 f: plane speed 6 → 30 px/f over 54 f (closed form 6n + 0.225n², linear acceleration with no ease-out), then 36 px/f for 26 f into the cut, about 1,900 px of travel (page at least plane length + 2,000 px); near-edge screen speed ≈ 6 → 34 px/f, under the blur pass throughout; rotateX 55°, perspective 1200 px, plane 2x frame height; caption words 6 f apart, landed by f40 of the flight; cut on the final frame.
- **Use when:** Showing the length or completeness of a page, document, feed or site in about a second without asking anyone to read it; a fast connective beat between two readable product shots, or the carrier for a change made mid-move, such as a theme switch.
- **Avoid when:** The content must be read, the page is short (it reads as a tilted card instead), or the frame is vertical and leaves too little runway; use it once per film.

### Mark docks into the app

`pd-mark-docks-into-app` · product demo · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, sting

An integration mark or icon travels to an app tile or page and settles overlapping its face, rising in front of it at the moment of contact, so it reads as plugging in.

- **Build:** Move the mark toward the tile centre minus a small offset (15-20% of the tile) over 25 f on E.outSoft so it decelerates into contact; at overlap (frame 17 of the approach) raise its z-index and translateZ above the tile, and let it come to rest on frame 25. On contact the tile answers with scale 1 + 0.02 · hitPulse(f − contact, 2, 3); the tile is a matte solid with a 1.5 px C.line edge and a soft neutral shadow. Shared-element variant: lift a small icon out of its row (scale 0.53 → 1 over 27 f on E.out while its tile inverts light/dark over 18 f), float it 45 f with a linear rotateZ 1.5° and rotateY 4° drift, then shrink it over 12 f on E.inOut into the logo slot of a page that swings in from the bottom right (perspective 1000 px, rotateX 55° → 40°, rotateZ −30° → −22° over 50 f on E.out). Position the icon through the page's own transform and, on the frame it reaches the slot, replace it with the page's own logo in one frame (decided with fd, identical transform) instead of crossfading the two copies.
- **Timing:** Approach 25 f on E.outSoft, overlap at f17, rest at f25; tile bump 2% (attack 2 f, tau 3, about 8 f). Variant: lift 27 f, colour invert 18 f, float 45 f, shrink 12 f on E.inOut, page swing 50 f on E.out, one-frame swap to the page logo on arrival.
- **Use when:** An integration, plug-in or works-inside claim; handing off from a settings screen into the platform it acts on.
- **Avoid when:** The mark would pass over text being read; the mark is also the end lockup (it would appear early, so dock an integration icon instead).

### Pin field pull-back

`pd-pin-field-pullback` · product demo · accent · energy medium · feature, launch, walkthrough

A map pulls back from a close view to reveal a field of location pins that drop in as accent marks and relax to ink, then a card grows out of the pin the cursor picks.

- **Build:** Scale the map group with k = lmix(2.2, 1, prog(f, s, s + 50, E.outSoft)) about the focus point. Pop the pins during the pull with SPR.micro (no visible overshoot: a field of pins is not a landing) on scale 0 → 1 and translateY −12 → 0 px, transform-origin at the bottom centre, with offsets from stagger(i, n, 30) so the whole group lands within 30 f; each pin arrives in C.accent and relaxes to C.ink over 24 f (mixColor). The cursor clicks one pin and its card grows from the pin tip (transform-origin at the pin, scale 0.6 → 1 over 12 f on E.out), with a leader line drawing over 8 f and its label sliding 25 px over 12 f on E.out.
- **Timing:** Pull 50 f on E.outSoft (first frame ≈ −7% scale per frame); pins ≈ 11 f each on SPR.micro, the group within 30 f (2-6 f apart); colour relax 24 f; card 12 f, leader 8 f, label 12 f.
- **Use when:** Location, coverage, store-finder or delivery features; any everywhere claim backed by real places.
- **Avoid when:** Fewer than about five locations; a map style busy enough to hide the pins; a route arc has already run on the same map.

### Headline becomes the product input

`pd-headline-becomes-input` · product demo · signature · energy medium · launch, feature, vertical

Without a cut the headline turns into the product: a caret appears in the gap between two words, swells into a capsule and widens into the input bar that shoves the words aside, or the sentence inside a card dissolves while the card reshapes into the input.

- **Build:** Lay out [wordL][slot][wordR] from data, centred, and bind each word's x to the slot's edges (wordL's right edge = cx − slotW/2 − gap) so the line reflows with no separate tween. Grow the slot as a 3 px C.accent caret (height 0 → line height over 6 f on E.out), hold 8 f, thicken to a 36 px capsule over 14 f, then widen to ≈ 92% of frame on E.rest over 60 f (edge peak ≈ 50 px/f, motion blur on) while its fill goes straight to the opaque input colour; the flanking words ride the edges and, once they pass 20 px/f, fade on E.smooth with blurOut as they leave frame. Populate container-first: icons, a C.mute placeholder and the send button fade in left to right 4 f apart over 12 f each with a 6 px arrive() rise, and the primary button fills last on a 16 f linear ramp. If the sentence already sits in a card, exit its words 6 f apart (the out props of src/fx/Words.tsx), tween the card's height to the input's over 30 f on E.out and fade the placeholder in over 16 f.
- **Timing:** Caret 6 f, hold 8 f, capsule 14 f, widen 60 f on E.rest (a short bar: 23 f in all on E.out); contents 12 f each at a 4 f stagger, button fill 16 f linear. Card variant: word exits 6 f apart, resize 30 f on E.out, placeholder 16 f.
- **Use when:** Bridging from message to demo in a type-led film; the product's core surface is an input, search or command bar.
- **Avoid when:** The product is not input-led; the headline has no natural gap; the bar would have to stay translucent over a busy backdrop (go straight to opaque).

### Shared element survives the page change

`pd-shared-element-page` · product demo · signature · energy medium · walkthrough, feature, launch

The cursor clicks a row; the page drains away except the row's icon (or the clicked card), which stays exactly in place while the next page assembles around it with a short zoom-out.

- **Build:** Duplicate the anchor (a row's icon, a card or a modal) into a top overlay at its exact screen rect. On the press frame fade page A to its background colour over 6 f on E.smooth and hold the lone anchor 2-4 f. Then mount page B at scale 1.2 about the anchor and settle it with lmix over 24 f on E.out, while the overlay interpolates from A's rect to B's (both computed from layout data, so FLIP by construction) and B's blocks fade in 2 f apart over 10 f. Cross-app variant: keep one card container mounted, take child A out through RackFocus to 8 px with opacity over 36 f, resize the card to the new aspect over 20 f on E.out, and bring child B in from 8 px over 24 f. Cut variant: keep the anchor fixed on a top layer while only the background layer switches on the cut frame, then drag the anchor into its new slot over 40 f on E.whip.
- **Timing:** Hover 12 f, press (pressAt), page A out 6 f, anchor alone 2-4 f, page B 1.2 → 1 over 24 f on E.out (≤ 50 px/f at 960 px from the anchor), block stagger 2 f over 10 f: about 48 f from click to settled. Cross-app: 36 f out, 20 f resize, 24 f in. Cut variant: anchor drag 40 f on E.whip.
- **Use when:** Navigating into a detail view, or carrying a piece of content between apps, where spatial continuity should make the product feel instant.
- **Avoid when:** Nothing exists in both states; the anchor is under about 40 px and cannot carry attention; it would need to travel more than a third of the frame (use a native transition).

### Tilted product plane flattens

`pd-tilted-plane-flattens` · product demo · signature · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

A real product page lies tipped back in perspective, rises toward the camera and rotates flat to face the viewer, landing the product as a frontal screen.

- **Build:** Give the page's parent perspective 1800-2000 px; on the page set transform-origin 50% 100% and tween translateY 270 → −60 px, rotateX 25° → 8° and scale 1 → 1.3 over 68 f on E.out, then drift linearly at about 3.5 px/f and leave on E.in. Resolve the last 8° → 0 as follow-through on its own E.out over 20 f, starting 6 f before the translate lands, so position and tilt settle at different moments. Hero version: hold the plane tilted for up to 34 f with progressive depth of field (4-6 horizontal bands, each a RackFocus at 0/2/4/6/8 px by distance from the focal row), then rotate rotateX and rotateZ to 0 over 80 f on E.glide while every band racks to sharp as the rotation reaches zero. Edge the page with a 1.5 px solid C.line hairline rather than a lit rim; an in-page headline may build with src/fx/Words.tsx while the plane still moves, but nothing is meant to be read until it lands.
- **Timing:** Rise 68 f on E.out: top edge ≈ 35 px/f on the first frame, ≈ 12 px/f by f4, ≈ 5.5 px/f by f8, then ≈ 3.5 px/f drift and an exit at ≈ 5.5 px/f on E.in; tilt follow-through 20 f, starting 6 f before the position lands; hero de-skew: hold ≤ 34 f, then 80 f on E.glide (peak edge speed ≈ 60-70 px/f at about 31%).
- **Use when:** Introducing a real web page or app screen as the real thing while keeping the camera alive; the first frontal look at the product.
- **Avoid when:** The UI must be read during the move; the plane would need more than about 30° of tilt (text shears and aliases); the same flatten ran within the last 10 s.
